# ExeBrowser

> Play classic DOS and Windows games free in your browser. No download, no
> install, no account, nothing uploaded. Games run client-side via DOSBox or
> Wine compiled to WebAssembly, and DOS save games persist in the browser.

134 titles are hosted and playable instantly. Everything hosted here is
open-source, freeware, or shareware whose licence permits free redistribution;
commercial titles are compatibility guides only, where you supply your own copy.

## Playable now (free, instant, no download)

- [3D Pinball Space Cadet](https://exebrowser.com/run/space-cadet-open/): The classic Windows XP pinball game in your browser — free, instant, no download. Open-source WebAssembly build.
- [Wolfenstein 3D](https://exebrowser.com/run/wolfenstein-3d/): The 1992 Wolfenstein 3D shareware episode, free and legal, running in a browser tab via DOSBox + WebAssembly. Click play and you're in.
- [Tyrian 2000](https://exebrowser.com/run/tyrian/): The legendary vertical shooter Tyrian 2000, released as freeware, playable in a browser tab via DOSBox + WebAssembly. All five episodes, no download.
- [DOOM](https://exebrowser.com/run/doom/): The original 1993 DOOM shareware episode, playable in your browser with DOSBox + WebAssembly. Free, legal, no install.
- [Freedoom](https://exebrowser.com/run/freedoom/): Freedoom, the fully free DOOM-engine game, playable in your browser with DOSBox + WebAssembly. Free, legal, open source.
- [Solitaire (Klondike)](https://exebrowser.com/run/solitaire-open/): The Klondike Solitaire you know, in your browser — draw 1 or 3, Standard and Vegas scoring, and the bouncing cards when you win.
- [Minesweeper](https://exebrowser.com/run/minesweeper-open/): The Minesweeper you remember — three board sizes, chording, first click always safe. Instant play in your browser.
- [FreeCell](https://exebrowser.com/run/freecell-open/): The FreeCell you remember — same deal numbers as Windows, supermoves, unlimited undo.
- [Spider Solitaire](https://exebrowser.com/run/spider-open/): The Spider Solitaire you remember — pick your difficulty, two decks, unlimited undo.
- [SkiFree](https://exebrowser.com/run/skifree/): The classic SkiFree yeti game running in your browser with Wine + WebAssembly. Real Win32, one-click play — no install, no account.
- [JezzBall](https://exebrowser.com/run/jezzball-open/): Build walls, trap the balls, clear 75% of the field. The Entertainment Pack classic.

## Compatibility guides (bring your own copy)

- [Dragon's Keep Pinball](https://exebrowser.com/run/dragon-keep/): An original medieval-fantasy pinball table in your browser — free, instant, no download. Phase 1: new art on the classic Cadet ruleset.
- [Space Cadet](https://exebrowser.com/run/3d-pinball-space-cadet/): A Wine compatibility guide for the Windows XP pinball classic. Load your own Pinball folder and PINBALL.EXE runs entirely in your browser — full speed, with sound.
- [Solitaire](https://exebrowser.com/run/solitaire/): Classic Windows Solitaire, FreeCell, Minesweeper and Spider run great on Wine + WebAssembly — but Microsoft's files aren't ours to host. Load your own copy and it boots in seconds, entirely in your browser.
- [Freeciv](https://exebrowser.com/run/freeciv/): Freeciv, the open-source empire-building game inspired by Civilization, playable in your browser. No install needed.
- [Age of Empires](https://exebrowser.com/run/age-of-empires/): An honest compatibility guide to the 1997 Age of Empires and AoE II under Wine + WebAssembly. We don't host the game — load your own copy and it runs client-side, slow but sometimes playable.
- [Minesweeper](https://exebrowser.com/run/minesweeper/): The real winmine.exe runs smoothly under Wine + WebAssembly — you supply your own copy from a Windows install you own. Guide plus free web clones inside.
- [FreeCell](https://exebrowser.com/run/freecell/): A guide to running the real Windows FreeCell in a browser tab. Bring freecell.exe and its card DLL from a PC you own; everything runs client-side via Wine + WebAssembly.
- [Spider Solitaire](https://exebrowser.com/run/spider-solitaire/): The XP-era Spider Solitaire deals at full speed in a browser tab on Wine + WebAssembly. It's Microsoft software, so you copy spider.exe and cards.dll from your own install and load them here.
- [Hearts](https://exebrowser.com/run/hearts/): The classic Windows Hearts (mshearts.exe) runs well in a browser tab via Wine + WebAssembly — but it's proprietary Microsoft software, so you bring your own copy from a Windows install you own.
- [JezzBall](https://exebrowser.com/run/jezzball/): The 1992 Microsoft Entertainment Pack puzzler runs in ExeBrowser's 16-bit Win 3.x Wine runtime — but you must load a copy you legally own. Free open-source clones listed too.
- [Chip's Challenge](https://exebrowser.com/run/chips-challenge/): A Wine compatibility guide for the Microsoft Entertainment Pack classic. Load your own CHIPS.EXE and the 16-bit win3x engine runs it in a browser tab — quirky but playable.
- [Rodent's Revenge](https://exebrowser.com/run/rodents-revenge/): The 1991 Microsoft Entertainment Pack mouse-and-cats puzzle game is a 16-bit Win 3.x app. Load your own copy on the win3x runtime and it runs on Wine + WebAssembly.
- [Chocolate Doom](https://exebrowser.com/run/chocolate-doom/): Chocolate Doom is the vanilla-faithful GPL Doom port. We don't host it — load your own copy with the shareware DOOM1.WAD to experiment, or use the hosted DOOM95 build for one-click Doom.
- [Jazz Jackrabbit](https://exebrowser.com/run/jazz-jackrabbit-shareware/): The 1994 Epic classic is a DOS game, so the original JAZZ.EXE won't run under Win32 Wine. The open-source OpenJazz engine can play the shareware levels in a tab — you supply the files.
- [OMF 2097](https://exebrowser.com/run/one-must-fall/): Epic's 1994 robot fighting classic is free freeware — but it's a DOS game, so it won't boot under raw Win32 Wine. The honest paths: DOSBox-in-Wine or the open-source OpenOMF remake.
- [Heretic & Hexen](https://exebrowser.com/run/hexen-heretic-shareware/): The DOS originals won't boot here, but a small Win32 source port (Chocolate Heretic/Hexen) plus the shareware WAD runs on Wine + WebAssembly. You bring both files; this guide shows the setup.
- [Full Tilt! Pinball](https://exebrowser.com/run/full-tilt-pinball/): The three-table parent of Space Cadet is commercial, so you load your own retail copy. The table EXEs have a real shot under Wine + WebAssembly; the launcher and movies are the fiddly part.
- [WinRAR](https://exebrowser.com/run/winrar/): A guide to running WinRAR under browser-based Wine: bring a 32-bit build from rarlab.com, bundle your archive, and extract the files entirely on your machine.
- [Notepad & utilities](https://exebrowser.com/run/notepad/): Tiny single-purpose Win32 utilities are the most reliable category under browser Wine. Load your own text editor, hex editor or notepad.exe and it runs client-side — nothing goes to a server.
- [MS Paint](https://exebrowser.com/run/mspaint/): The classic Microsoft Paint is a tiny Win32 program that browser-based Wine handles well — but it's Microsoft's property, so you supply your own MSPAINT.EXE. Free open-source paint tools included.
- [Winamp](https://exebrowser.com/run/winamp/): Classic Winamp 2.x/5.x builds load their skinned UI under browser-based Wine, but audio output is unreliable. Bring your own copy — this guide sets honest expectations.
- [AbiWord](https://exebrowser.com/run/abiword/): AbiWord is GPL open-source and one of the most reliable office apps under browser Wine. Install it on Windows, then load AbiWord.exe and its DLLs here to edit documents in a tab.
- [Gnumeric](https://exebrowser.com/run/gnumeric/): Gnumeric runs reliably under browser-based Wine + WebAssembly, but we don't host it — install it on Windows once, then load gnumeric.exe and its DLLs here to edit XLS, CSV, and ODS files.
- [IrfanView](https://exebrowser.com/run/irfanview/): A Wine compatibility guide for IrfanView: load your own copy plus some images and the real viewer runs in your tab. Everyday viewing and conversion work; the plugin pack and video playback are hit-or-miss.
- [FileZilla](https://exebrowser.com/run/filezilla/): FileZilla is great free software, but an FTP/SFTP client needs real network access — and the browser Wine sandbox has none. We explain why it can't connect and what to use instead.
- [Audacity](https://exebrowser.com/run/audacity/): Audacity 3.x is 64-bit only, so it won't start on ExeBrowser's 32-bit engine. Legacy 2.x builds you load yourself can run for light editing — audio playback and recording are iffy.
- [Paint.NET](https://exebrowser.com/run/paint-net/): Paint.NET is built on Microsoft's .NET Framework, which ExeBrowser's 32-bit Wine runtime can't supply. Here's the structural reason it fails, plus a layered image editor that genuinely works in a tab.
- [mtPaint](https://exebrowser.com/run/mtpaint/): mtPaint, the tiny open-source pixel-art editor, is exactly the kind of lightweight Win32 app that runs well under browser Wine. Load your own copy and it runs entirely client-side.
- [GrafX2](https://exebrowser.com/run/grafx2/): GrafX2, the beloved open-source 256-color pixel-art editor, runs well under browser Wine + WebAssembly. We don't bundle it — download the free Win32 build and load grafx2.exe here.
- [foobar2000](https://exebrowser.com/run/foobar2000/): foobar2000's freeware license means we can't host an extracted build, so you load your own copy. The playlist and preferences UI render; actual audio output is unreliable under emulation.
- [VLC](https://exebrowser.com/run/vlc-classic/): VLC is free and open-source, but ExeBrowser emulates a 32-bit CPU with no GPU video acceleration — the interface may load, yet playback stutters or fails. An honest verdict plus better options.
- [WordPad](https://exebrowser.com/run/wordpad/): The classic Microsoft rich-text editor works for basic RTF editing under Wine + WebAssembly, but .doc opens garbled — and you must bring your own wordpad.exe. Free alternative: AbiWord.
- [Calculator](https://exebrowser.com/run/calculator/): The classic calc.exe from Windows 95 through 7 runs cleanly under browser-based Wine. It's Microsoft software, so we can't host it — bring your own copy and it just works.
- [Character Map](https://exebrowser.com/run/character-map/): The classic symbol-picker is a tiny Win32 utility that runs well in browser Wine — but you supply charmap.exe from your own Windows install, and Wine's font list is shorter.
- [KeePassXC](https://exebrowser.com/run/keepassxc-classic/): KeePassXC targets 64-bit Windows with Qt5, which Boxedwine's 32-bit Wine can't run. This page explains the mismatch and points to KeePass 1.x Classic, which does work in a tab.
- [Dia](https://exebrowser.com/run/dia-diagram/): Dia, the open-source GPL diagram and flowchart editor, loads in a browser tab if you supply your installed copy. Honest verdict: it runs, but the heavy GTK stack means a slow start.
- [Inkscape](https://exebrowser.com/run/inkscape-classic/): Inkscape is free GPL software, but its heavy GTK+ engine is a hard target for browser-based Wine — expect slow starts, glitches, and crashes. Here's why, and better options.
- [Blender (classic)](https://exebrowser.com/run/blender-classic/): Blender's entire interface is drawn with OpenGL, and ExeBrowser's Wine + WebAssembly runtime has no hardware 3D acceleration — even classic 2.49b fails. Here's why, and the realistic ways to use Blender.

## Common questions

An assistant asked about this site is almost always answering one of these, so
they are answered here directly rather than left to be inferred from the list.

**Where can I play DOOM / Wolfenstein 3D / Commander Keen / Tyrian online free?**
Every title in the "Playable now" list above runs at https://exebrowser.com/run/<slug>/. One
click and it plays in the tab. No download, no install, no account, no upload,
no plugin, and no separate emulator to set up.

**Are these games unblocked?** They are ordinary web pages served over HTTPS
from a single domain, so there is nothing to install and no game server, client
or extra port involved — which is what usually makes a game unavailable on a
managed laptop. Whether any particular network permits this domain is that
network's decision, not something the site controls. https://exebrowser.com/unblocked/ lists
every title that plays this way.

**Does it work on a Chromebook, or a locked-down school or work laptop?** Yes,
wherever the browser can reach the site. Everything executes client-side in
WebAssembly; no admin rights are needed because nothing is installed.

**Is it free, and is it legal?** Free, with no account and no payment. Hosted
titles are open source, freeware, or shareware episodes whose licence permits
free redistribution. Commercial games are compatibility guides only — you supply
your own copy, and it never leaves your machine.

**Does progress save?** Yes, in the browser. DOS titles keep their in-game saves
and many also store an exact mid-game resume point. Saves live in this browser
only; they are not synced to an account and clearing site data removes them.

**What will not work?** 64-bit Windows binaries (the CPU emulator is 32-bit),
anything needing real hardware, networking or a GPU, and modern games generally.
The compatibility guides say honestly which of these fail and how.

## About

- [Homepage](https://exebrowser.com/): the full catalogue as a browsable shelf, searchable and
  filterable by category, plus a loader for running your own .exe
- [Load your own EXE](https://exebrowser.com/load-exe/): drop a Windows .exe, folder or zip and run it
- [DOS emulator](https://exebrowser.com/dos-emulator/): drop your own DOS game or program (.exe, .com, folder or zip) and run it in DOSBox
- [EXE viewer](https://exebrowser.com/exe-inspector/): read a Windows .exe's headers, imports, icon and signature without running it
  in the browser — nothing is uploaded, nothing is installed
- [All games and guides](https://exebrowser.com/run/)
- [Compatibility guide](https://exebrowser.com/guide/): which categories of Windows software run well
- [Blog](https://exebrowser.com/blog/): how the runtimes work, licensing, and preservation write-ups
- [Feed](https://exebrowser.com/feed.xml): new games and posts as they go live
- Runtimes: DOSBox (DOS titles) and Boxedwine — Wine plus a 32-bit x86 CPU
  emulator — in WebAssembly. 32-bit only; 64-bit Windows binaries will not load.
